findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_request, cancel_request · Private data: search_businesses, get_business, get_available_times, create_request, get_request_status, cancel_request · Public sink: get_business, get_available_times, create_request, cancel_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_request, cancel_request · Private data: search_businesses, get_business, get_available_times, create_request, get_request_status, cancel_request · Public sink: get_business, get_available_times, create_request, cancel_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

detail: Tool "search_businesses" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Find local businesses on Loomivo by what they do (e.g. 'dentist') and town. Returns which can be booked, ordered from or asked for a quote online; listed: true means a free listing that takes requests in the customer's words, confirmed by the owner within 24 hours." → after: "Search verified local businesses on Loomivo by what they do and where. Use this first when the customer has not named a specific business (e.g. 'a dentist in Karaikal'); if they named one, search for its name. Returns up to 20 businesses with their slug (needed by get_business, get_available_times a"

remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
